sections.text:
15.1 Basics
The pMRP functionality doesn’t require any configuration settings at all. This means
that you can use pMRP right away as long as the proper operational MRP configuration
is in place, such as a valid plant, MRP controllers, and so on. The pMRP functionality
does, however, need the following basic master data and transactional data to already
be in place:
 Material master
Any MRP-relevant material can be used for a pMRP simulation.

sections.title: Setup
sections.text:
15.2 Setup
 BOM
A valid BOM with the BOM usage set to 1—Production should exist for a material that
will be used in a simulation.
 Work center
The work center used in a simulation should have at least one capacity relevant for
finite scheduling.
 Routing
A valid routing should exist, and the operation in the bottleneck resource operation
should be relevant to capacity planning.
 Production version
At least one valid production version referring to the BOM and routing should exist.
If there is more than one valid production version, then you can change the source
of supply during the simulation.
 Purchasing info record
A purchasing info record is a one-to-one material-to-supplier relationship that is
needed for the pMRP process so that the system can assign at least one source of
supply to each material that is procured.
 Planned independent requirements
PIRs for the relevant materials must be maintained.
All of this data is also used by MRP for planning materials.
Before you start to use pMRP, all of the relevant master data must be available. As one
of the main objectives behind pMRP is to allow the user to check whether there is
enough capacity to produce the forecasted quantities, it’s very important to correctly
set up the routing and the work center with the standard values and the proper formu-
las.
From a transactional data perspective, the main input for pMRP is a demand plan,
which is represented by PIRs (Transaction MD61). The planning strategy used isn’t rele-
vant because it supports any requirement type, and you can use an active or an inactive
PIR version. When choosing an inactive version, the capacity planner will need to select
the version number during simulation creation.
15.2 Setup
The first step in the pMRP process is to create a pMRP simulation, wherein you as a
planner can choose to restrict a set of master data for simulation purposes. When you
create a simulation, you can select which top-level materials, components, or work cen-
ters will be considered for pMRP. In pMRP, the planning will happen during the simula-
tion creation itself. With pMRP, you will be able to process the simulation immediately
after the creation is finished and will not have to wait for a planning run. The pMRP

15 Predictive Material and Resource Planning
840
process uses simplified planning logic, in which all materials use a deterministic MRP
and a lot-for-lot procedure.
Before creating the simulation, you must ensure that the relevant master data has been
created. You must also have created the PIRs, since they will be the main input into the
pMRP simulation. The system will plan the selected materials and determine the work
center capacity requirements based on those PIRs.
A word of caution here: when a simulation is created, master data will be copied into it,
so subsequent changes to master data may not be considered.
Creating a pMRP simulation is basically a background job that you can schedule
through the Schedule pMRP Simulation Creation app. You can also use this application
to manage background jobs that are already finished, scheduled, or in process.
As shown in Figure 15.2, an icon in the Log column will show the status of the finished
background executions, and another icon appears in the Results column. Choosing the
icon in the Log column will show the details of success, warning, or error messages that
may have been triggered during each step of simulation creation.
You can create, copy, and delete a simulation creation (although deletion is only possi-
ble for scheduled jobs). To create a new application job, choose Create on the screen
shown in Figure 15.2, which will bring up the screen shown in Figure 15.3.
Figure 15.2 Application Jobs
On the screen shown in Figure 15.3. you can use the dropdown list in the Job Template
field to choose from the following three job templates, which have different selection
criteria:
 Creation of pMRP Data via Top-Level Materials
In this template, object selection is based on the material master, so the selection cri-
teria will be focused on material master information, such as material number, MRP
controller, and low-level code. The system will look for PIRs for the relevant materi-
als and run simplified MRP to determine the required quantity for each level and the
capacity allocated in the work center.
© 

841
15.2 Setup
 Creation of pMRP Data via Components
Selecting this template will enable you to select components as inputs for creating
the simulation. In this case, pMRP will use the BOM to find relevant upper-level
materials and look for demands for these materials.
 Creation of pMRP Data via Work Center
In this template, object selection is based on the work center, so the selection criteria
will be focused on the work center. The system will look for capacity requirements in
the selected work centers and then identify the top-level materials and the respec-
tive PIRs.
For this example, you choose the first option from the dropdown list in Figure 15.3 1
and then click the Step 2 button.
Figure 15.3 Scheduling pMRP
Then, in the Scheduling Options section 2, you define whether the job will be executed
immediately or scheduled to run on a future date. The creation of the pMRP simulation
will be executed only once; therefore, it should not be executed as a periodic job, and the
Recurrence Pattern value will be set to Single-Run by default. Then, click the Step 3 but-
ton on the screen shown in Figure 15.3 to make the screen shown in Figure 15.4 appear.
In the Parameter Section of the screen shown in Figure 15.4, fill in the ID for Reference
Plan and Simulation ID fields, which are used to identify the simulation. You should use
unique values; the reference ID and simulation ID cannot be the same. The ID for the

15 Predictive Material and Resource Planning
842
reference plan will represent the set of master data selected according to the selection
criteria, and you can add new simulations later under the same reference ID. Then, in
the Parameter Section, select the Bucket Category (daily, weekly, or monthly buckets)
and the start and end date for the simulation.
Figure 15.4 Parameters Selection in pMRP Scheduling, Part 1
In the Limitations section, there are more fields you can use to restrict the selection.
You can use these fields to ensure that pMRP will be executed only for materials with a
specific BOM, routing, or material status, or for a BOM or task list usage.
Then, scroll down the screen shown in Figure 15.4 until the screen shown in Figure 15.5
appears.
The Object Selection section of the screen shown in Figure 15.5 contains the fields that
you will use to select materials or work centers. Depending on the job template you’ve
selected, you’ll see material-related fields (such as the Material, Plant, MRP Controller,
Material Type, and Low-Level Code) or work center-related fields (such as Work Center,
Work Center Category, and Person Responsible) here. You can also define whether stock
transfers will be considered in the scenario and which plants and which work centers
from those supplying plants should be considered in the simulation.
Finally, in the Document Data section, you choose whether the opening stock will be zero,
whether it will be the safety stock or the actual material stock at the plant, whether an
inactive PIR version will be considered instead of the active version, and whether the sim-
ple discontinuation will be considered.
You define all of these settings in the reference plan while creating the simulation.
You cannot change them later, when you’re adding new simulations to the same ref-
erence plan. Once you click the Schedule button, the background job to create the new
simulation will be scheduled. Depending on the number of materials you select for
the simulation, the job may take some time because it executes an actual planning
© 

843
15.2 Setup
run. We highly recommend that you first check the completeness and correctness of
the data you’ve maintained by choosing Check; the message that will appear at the
bottom of the screen will confirm whether the application job can be scheduled.
Figure 15.5 Parameters Selection in pMRP Scheduling, Part 2
Figure 15.6 shows the details of the simulation creation logs, including the success and
error messages that have been triggered. When you choose the icon in the Results col-
umn shown previously in Figure 15.2, the screen will jump into the spool, which dis-
plays a list of the materials and work centers selected for the simulation.
Figure 15.6 Application Log
After you create the pMRP simulation, you will be able to process the simulation in the
Process pMRP Simulations app, as discussed in the next section.

15 Predictive Material and Resource Planning
844

sections.title: Managing pMRP
sections.text:
15.3 Managing pMRP
In the Process pMRP Simulations app, you as a planner will actually work with the sim-
ulation, analyze the planning results, identify and resolve capacity issues, and validate
the forecast you’ve created. Once the simulation is processed, you can release the
results to operational planning in the form of PIRs. Then, the forecast can become rele-
vant to MRP.
When you open this app, it will display a list of all the created simulations, including
the total number of capacity issues, the delivery performance, and the simulation sta-
tus. These appear in separate columns. The number of capacity issues represents the
total number of buckets in which a capacity issue was identified, and the delivery per-
formance represents the percentage of the originally planned forecast that can be ful-
filled. For example, if a capacity issue is found and the forecast quantity was reduced to
resolve the issue, then the delivery performance will be adjusted accordingly.
The Simulation Status column is related to the results of the simulation creation; if the
status is Created with Warnings or Fatal Errors, you can refer to the simulation creation
logs shown in Figure 15.7.
Figure 15.7 Processing pMRP Simulations
In this application, you also have the option to copy, rename, or delete an existing sim-
ulation or override errors. When you copy a simulation, it will be linked to the same ref-
erence data as the original simulation. Also, you can choose whether to copy data from
the simulation or from the reference data, as shown in Figure 15.8. If you choose to copy
from the simulation, then changes already made to the simulation will also be copied;
if you choose to copy from the reference data, changes made to the simulation will not
be considered and the original forecast quantities from the reference data will be cop-
ied. You can also add a percentage for the Overload Tolerance value so that pMRP will
not consider a work center overload until reaching the tolerance.
© 

845
15.3 Managing pMRP
When you choose one of the simulations, the Demand Plan Simulation screen will
appear (see Figure 15.9). This screen shows the lines with the materials selected for the
simulation, and each column represents the forecast quantity for a specific bucket.
Some cells are highlighted in red because there is an issue with a capacity overload in
the work center: the forecasted quantities will require more time to be produced than
is available with the current shift schedules in the work centers. The capacity issue may
be related to either top-level materials or a semifinished product in the BOM’s lower
levels.
Figure 15.8 Copying pMRP Simulation
Figure 15.9 Demand Plan Simulation
The Demand Plan Simulation screen shows the number of capacity issues, but there’s
no issue with delivery performance. The number of capacity issues will not necessarily
match the number of highlighted cells; two or more cells may be highlighted due to the
same capacity issue in a specific work center. In this example, the delivery performance
is still 100% because the originally forecasted quantities have not yet been changed,
but this number may change when a supply chain planner tries to resolve the capacity
issues caused by the forecasted quantities. We’ll cover that scenario later in this chap-
ter.
On this screen, you choose from the following options in the Quantities Displayed
dropdown list:

15 Predictive Material and Resource Planning
846
 Simulation Only
This column shows the forecast quantities related to the simulation.
 Reference/Simulation
Two columns will appear: the original quantity from the reference and the simula-
tion quantities. With this option, you can compare the changes made to the simula-
tion with the original quantities to form a better estimation of the impact of the
changes over the originally forecasted quantity.
 Delta of the Reference and Simulation
This column only shows the difference between the reference and the simulation.
This view also helps you estimate the impacts of the changes you’ve made in the
simulation.
If you choose Capacity Plan Simulation from the Simulation Views dropdown list
located in the top right-hand corner of Figure 15.9, a different screen will appear. It
focuses on work center capacity, as shown in Figure 15.10. The upper part of the screen
shows a list of the work centers selected for this simulation, with the total number of
hours allocated and the remaining capacity of the work centers for every month. In the
lower part of the screen, a chart shows a graphical overview of the work centers’ possi-
ble load and the overload. In the chart bars, the green area represents the feasible load
(the capacity requirements that can be fulfilled with the current work center capacity),
and the red area represents the capacity overload that is causing the issue.
Figure 15.10 Capacity Plan Simulation
In the capacity plan simulation, two buttons correspond to the two alternatives for
dealing with the capacity issues:
 Disregard Capacity Issues
The pMRP process will simply ignore all the existing capacity issues for the selected
work center. The total number of capacity issues will be reduced, and the cells will no
longer be highlighted in red.
© 

847
15.3 Managing pMRP
 Change Available Capacity
You can change the work center’s available capacity to allow for a capacity overload.
When you choose this option, a popup will appear (see Figure 15.11), wherein you can
choose months and the percentage of overload allowed. Months with a capacity
issue will be highlighted in red, and the system will also propose a capacity utiliza-
tion that can resolve the capacity issue for each month. Be sure to select one or more
relevant months from the Months to Show dropdown so that the system brings up
the option to make changes to the existing capacities.
Figure 15.11 Changing Available Capacity
On both the Capacity Plan Simulation screen and the Demand Plan Simulation screen,
if you choose the Inspector view, the system will display a side panel with additional
information about the selected object (see Figure 15.12). When you’re using the Inspec-
tor on the Capacity Plan Simulation screen, the inspected objects will be the work cen-
ter and the capacity allocated for the selected month, and the Inspector will also show
the top-level materials related to the capacity allocated in the work center.
Figure 15.12 Inspector Panel

15 Predictive Material and Resource Planning
848
If you use the Inspector tool from the Demand Plan Simulation screen, then the
inspected objects will be the material and the quantity forecasted for the selected
month. The tool will also display the capacity issues related to the forecast created for
this specific top-level material, even if they’re caused by a material in the lower BOM
levels. Also, when you’re using the Inspector from the Demand Plan Simulation screen,
a link will appear that, when clicked, will bring up the multilevel material simulation
for the selected demand.
Figure 15.12 shows the Inspector view for a demand plan simulation. It includes links to
the Multi-Level Material Simulation and the capacity plan simulation for the work cen-
ters with capacity issues. (The latter is not shown, but scrolling down will reveal it).
The screen in Figure 15.13 will appear when you select the Simulation Components
option from the Simulation Views dropdown list in Figure 15.12. This view is a summary
of various components and their availability in the chosen time bucket. (Here, it’s the
monthly time bucket.)
Figure 15.13 Simulation Components
If you click the Multi-Level Material Simulation link, the system will bring up a screen
with a complete BOM for a specific bucket, including the details of the required and
missing quantities for each material in each BOM level (see Figure 15.14). There may be
a number of issues and a number of sources of supply available for each material;
therefore, it’s possible to identify on exactly which BOM level there is a capacity issue.
Figure 15.14 shows the details of the multilevel material simulation, and it indicates that
several materials have capacity issues.
In the multilevel material simulation, it’s also possible to resolve the capacity issues
for top-level and lower-level materials. For materials with several sources of supply
(and thus with several valid production versions), you can select the Change Source of
© 

849
15.3 Managing pMRP
Supply option and then select a different production version. When you choose this
option, a popup appears (see Figure 15.15) in which you can distribute the forecasted
quantity among the different production versions that are available for the selected
material. Here, you’ll see an overview of the available capacity for each source of supply
and a proposed distribution of the forecast quantity among the different production
versions. Also, you can manually define the quantity distribution or select the Adopt
Proposal option (see Figure 15.15) to automatically adopt the proposed distribution.
Figure 15.14 Multilevel Material Simulation
Figure 15.15 Changing Source of Supply
Figure 15.16 shows that the demand for the month of January 2025 is being shifted to Feb-
ruary 2025 (preproduction) to balance the capacity overload at the given work center.

15 Predictive Material and Resource Planning
850
Figure 15.16 Shifting Top-Level Demand
The Pull In Quantity option shown in Figure 15.14 will enable you as a capacity and
materials planner to either preproduce an in-house-produced material or request early
procurement of an externally procured material (see Figure 15.17).
Figure 15.17 Preproduction or Early Procurement of Components
If there are still any unresolved issues that need attention or the action of a capacity
planner, then you can evaluate these issues in the Issue List (see Figure 15.18). Here, you
can choose to disregard the capacity overload issues you face.
© 

851
15.3 Managing pMRP
Figure 15.18 Issue List
Figure 15.19 is the Demand Plan Simulation screen, which shows that reducing the orig-
inal PIRs leads to poorer delivery performance. For this example, previously, delivery
performance was 100%, but after a reduction of the PIRs for a few months, delivery per-
formance has correspondingly decreased to 86%. The right-hand side of the screen
shows the complete log or history of all the changes made to this pMRP plan.
Figure 15.19 Delivery Performance Impacted
Tips and Tricks
If you choose one of the many KPIs displayed at the header level in Figure 15.19, a popup
will appear and show you more details about the issues facing the KPI. From this
popup, you as a planner can navigate to the detailed list, which is basically an issue list,
to better understand and address the issues in hand.

15 Predictive Material and Resource Planning
852
On any of the main screens of the Process pMRP Simulations app, the Simulation Sum-
mary button is available, and clicking it gives you an overview of all the changes made
while you’ve been processing the simulation. The following change categories will be
shown:
 Changes in Demand
 Changes in Capacity
 Preproduction or Early Procurement
 Changes in Source of Supply
 Unresolved Issues
 Disregarded Capacity Issues
Figure 15.20 shows the Simulation Summary screen, which has tabs for the different
change categories and the total number in each category. You can also export this table
to a spreadsheet so that you can further discuss and validate the forecast changes.
Figure 15.20 Simulation Summary

sections.title: Releasing Results to Operative Material Requirements Planning
sections.text:
15.4 Releasing Results to Operative Material Requirements Planning
Once the simulation process is complete and you’ve identified and resolved all of the
capacity issues, or if you as a capacity planner decide to disregard them or compromise
on delivery performance, then you can release the pMRP simulation. You accomplish
this by choosing the Release button on the initial screen of the Process pMRP Simula-
tions app. This brings up a popup (see Figure 15.21) in which you can confirm whether
the simulation can be released, and the forecast will be transferred to the top-level
materials in an inactive version 01, even if you created the simulation with active PIRs
as references. The option to transfer PIRs into an active version also exists in the same
© 

853
15.4 Releasing Results to Operative Material Requirements Planning
popup (see Version Active: Yes). Also, as mentioned at the beginning of this chapter, in
the latest version of SAP S/4HANA, DDMRP can also consider PIRs for the buffer calcu-
lation. This means that the pMRP simulation results will be an input for DDMRP. When
the simulation is released, if there are DDMRP materials in the BOM’s lower levels, then
PIRs will be created for DDMRP materials, even if there was no PIR for those materials
before the simulation creation. Therefore, the buffer calculation will take into consider-
ation any demand variability that can be anticipated by the forecast.
Furthermore, you can copy the inactive PIRs created by DDMRP to the active version in
Transaction MD70. Alternatively, you can simply check the Active flag in Transaction
MD62 to activate PIRs. When you release a simulation, the Show Log option (not
shown) will provide a complete log of the PIRs that are transferred. If you need to, you
can check the Subassembly Components box to bring up the option to transfer the sub-
components of the main assembly in the chosen version (see Requirements Version* in
Figure 15.21). Furthermore, the pMRP tool in SAP S/4HANA 2023 offers even more
options for the system to consider materials that are managed via Kanban (discussed
in Chapter 9) and even non-MRP materials.
Figure 15.21 Releasing pMRP Simulation
Figure 15.22 shows the updated status of the pMRP simulation that has been processed,
and the Simulation Status denotes that it is Released.

15 Predictive Material and Resource Planning
854
Figure 15.22 Processed Simulation Released to Operative MRP
You access the screen shown in Figure 15.23 via Transaction MD62. It shows that Mate-
rial 2269 in Plant 1710 now has updated PIRs transferred through pMRP simulation.
Because this PIR is now in operative planning, it’s ready for the MRP run.
Figure 15.23 Updated Planned Independent Requirements
Next, refer to Figure 15.21 again. If you checked the Capacity Changes Proposals box
during pMRP release, then the system will be able to adopt the capacity changes you
made during the simulation and also update the work center capacity using the Mass
Maintenance of the Work Center Capacities app (see Figure 15.24). When you open this
app, you can select the pMRP Change Proposal flag to see a list of all the changes pro-
posed by pMRP simulations. When you select one of the lines, you’ll be able to see the
details of the capacity change proposed by the pMRP simulation, including the month
and the proposed capacity utiliztion. Or, you can simply reject the proposal if it’s not
possible to implement it.
Figure 15.24 Changes to pMRP in the Mass Maintenance of Work Center Capacities App
© 

855

sections.title: Using Flexible Constraints
sections.text:
15.5 Using Flexible Constraints
15.5 Using Flexible Constraints
The pMRP functionality allows you as a planner to define flexible constraints for prod-
ucts. For example, you can define that a maximum quantity of a certain material can be
produced or purchased in any given time period (week or month). If this quantity is
exceeded, pMRP will generate an alert when processing the pMRP simulation. You can
also define flexible constraints for a single material or multiple materials, and you can
used them for materials produced in house, externally procured materials, or stock
transfer materials. The available periodicities are weeks and months.
To define a flexible constraint, you use the Define Flexible Constraints app (see Figure
15.25 1). In this example, we use the same material, 2269, in plant 1710, and we have
defined a constraint that whenever the production quantity is more than 75 pieces (PC)
during the period from August 2024 to February 2025, then the system should consider
this constraint while processing pMRP. When you’ve scheduled the pMRP and you pro-
ceed to process it, the system will show the Violated Constraints (see Figure 15.25 2).
Figure 15.25 Flexible Constraint

15 Predictive Material and Resource Planning
856
Since pMRP is an interactive tool, any changes made during processing will immediately
be reflected. For example, in 2, if you reduce the quantity of Material 2269 below 75 PC,
then the system will accordingly update (reduce) the status of the violated constraints.
Clicking on the Violated Constraints field will bring up detailed information on all the
constraints that have been violated.

sections.title: Summary
sections.text:
15.6 Summary
The pMRP functionality is the latest innovation in SAP S/4HANA, and it offers simula-
tion capabilities that can be used by production and capacity planners to make fore-
casting from a work center capacity point of view both practical and achievable. With
pMRP, a supply chain planner can change forecasted quantities and evaluate the
results, test different sources of supply for different products, and consider the prepro-
duction of certain critical products to avoid a capacity overload in a specific month. The
pMRP functionality is still in the development phase, and more innovations are
expected to be delivered in future releases of SAP S/4HANA.
The next chapter covers capacity requirements planning, which includes capacity eval-
uation and capacity leveling.
